findings_that_changed_the_procedure.finding: G: was the obvious backup target by free space (164 GiB) but is a partition of the SAME physical disk as F:. Backing up there would have produced a receipt claiming a cold backup that shares a single point of failure with the source.
findings_that_changed_the_procedure.action: backup redirected to E: on Disk 0

findings_that_changed_the_procedure.finding: core.longpaths is UNSET. `git ls-files --others` emits warnings and SILENTLY SKIPS directories past MAX_PATH. git enumerated 6372 files under 20_engineering; the filesystem actually holds 6568 - a 196-file blind spot, and 439 files exceed 260 chars (longest 348).
findings_that_changed_the_procedure.action: the SHA-256 manifest is built from an os.walk over a Win32 extended-length (\\?\) path, never from git enumeration

findings_that_changed_the_procedure.finding: The first robocopy invocation appeared to succeed (shell reported exit 0) but copied NOTHING: Git Bash MSYS path conversion rewrote the /E switch into 'E:/', so robocopy saw an invalid third parameter and aborted with its own exit 16. The log and destination did not exist.
findings_that_changed_the_procedure.action: re-run under MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1; destination existence and the robocopy summary block are now checked rather than trusting the shell exit code
